Senior Analytics Engineer, Analytics & Insights 

London, UK (Hybrid, 2 days in office) 

Material Bank is the world's largest material marketplace for the architecture and design industry. Operating in 37 countries, our platform has become the standard for design professionals around the globe. Every day, Material Bank connects thousands of designers with tens of thousands of materials from leading brands. Material Bank is the fastest and most powerful way for design professionals to search, sample, and specify materials. 

About the role 

We are looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to join Analytics & Insights, the team that owns Material Bank's analytics data layer, internal reporting, and data products that support our teams and brand partners. 

This is a hands-on technical role for someone who wants to own how analytics get built. You will take approved metric definitions and business questions and turn them into the models and metric logic in Snowflake and dbt, the dashboards, and the semantic layer and data products people use every day. 

You will own the analytics engineering for key areas of the business: understanding what needs to be measured, building the models, validating the logic, delivering the reporting, and keeping it accurate and reliable over time. You will work across multiple departments and across our data products, including embedded analytics for brands. The work varies day to day, and as a team we contribute to everything. 

What we require 

  • Ownership, end to end. You own what you build, from the first stakeholder conversation to the model, the dashboard, and the fix when something breaks. 
  • Precision and attention to detail. You understand the nuance behind a number, verify before you publish, and produce work that leaders and brand partners can trust without checking. 
  • Appetite for hard work. We are a small, ambitious team with a lot of goals. The work is demanding and the hours vary with what needs to get done. We are upfront about that because it is what the role is. 

What you'll do 

  • Own the analytics engineering for assigned business domains, translating metric definition through data model, dashboard, and insight. 
  • Design, build, and maintain documented, production-quality dbt models in Snowflake that turn approved metric definitions into reliable, reusable models and semantic definitions, and power reporting, self-serve, automation, and AI. 
  • Identify and resolve technical inconsistencies in metric logic so the business runs on one certified source of truth. 
  • Build a small set of high-value dashboards in Tableau (and Sigma, as we evolve the stack). 
  • Contribute to the semantic layer so certified metrics are reusable across BI tools, Snowflake Cortex, and embedded analytics. 
  • Automate recurring analytics work, with the tests and monitoring that keep it trustworthy. 
  • Partner with analysts and stakeholders to interpret data, build context, and surface risks before they are asked. 
  • Contribute to brand-facing data products used by account teams and manufacturer partners. 

What you'll bring 

  • 5+ years in analytics engineering, data analytics, or a similar technical analytics role, owning data models and reporting that a business relies on. 
  • Expert SQL on large and complex datasets. You write clean, efficient queries and can debug someone else's logic as easily as your own. 
  • Strong hands-on Snowflake and dbt (or a comparable modern data stack), including dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing, and documentation. 
  • Strong Tableau skills. Sigma, Looker, or similar a plus. 
  • Strong judgment on metric design: grain, denominators, filters, time zones, deduplication, and the ways a correct number can still mislead. 
  • Commercial sense and curiosity. You want to understand why a number matters, can explain what a change means for the business, and hold a position under questioning. 
  • An automation mindset. When you see something repetitive or fragile, your instinct is to find a better way to build it. 
  • Comfort working across several domains at once, prioritizing your own work, and managing stakeholders directly. 
  • Clear, concise communication and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences. 

Preferred 

Helpful, not required: 

  • Python for automation and data validation 
  • Marketplace, e-commerce, or B2B SaaS analytics 
  • Event and behavioral data (Segment, GA4, or similar) 
  • Semantic layers and AI-assisted analytics (Snowflake Cortex, dbt Semantic Layer, or similar) 
  • Embedded or customer-facing analytics (ClickHouse, Preset, or similar) 
  • Experimentation and causal methods: A/B testing, cohort analysis, difference-in-differences 
  • Catalog, product attribute, or search data 

What success looks like 

In your first 30 days you understand the stack, the models, the people, and the priorities in your domains, and you have your first dbt change merged. 

By 60 days you are producing real work independently: agreed metric definitions implemented, your first certified models and dashboards in use, and a plan for the first manual workflow you will automate. 

By 90 days stakeholders treat you as their analytics partner rather than a request queue. Your models are trusted, your dashboards are used without hand-holding, and your automation is reducing real manual effort.

The Regional Operations Director is accountable for the operational effectiveness of the EMEA region. Reporting to the Global Chief Transformation and Operations Officer, you'll translate the global operating model into practical, market-specific execution — building the structure, governance and performance focus needed to strengthen operational control and support scalable growth.

You'll lead a regional operations team, partner closely with regional and global leadership, and act as the key connector between regional execution and global capability. The role calls for a leader equally comfortable setting strategic direction and solving complex operational problems hands-on — someone who turns data into action, builds high-performing teams, and keeps commercial performance firmly in focus.

What you will be doing: 

 

Regional operational leadership

  • Set clear priorities, accountabilities and ways of working for the EMEA Regional Operations function.
  • Build the structure, rhythm and capability needed to improve client delivery, business performance and regional growth.
  • Act as the senior operational partner to Regional Leadership on risks, performance, capacity and improvement priorities.

Client delivery operations

  • Own the operational run model for EMEA clients — including cadence, governance, issue resolution and escalation management.
  • Partner with Account Leadership to ensure delivery risks are visible, blockers are resolved quickly and client teams are set up to deliver effectively.
  • Ensure regional clients are mobilised and supported through consistent operating standards and reliable delivery controls.

Governance, cadence and decision management

  • Own the regional governance rhythm: forums, communications, decision-making and performance reviews.
  • Ensure decisions are made at the right level, escalations are routed effectively and regional context is represented in relevant global and regional forums.
  • Drive clear actions, accountability and follow-through across the function.

Operating model execution

  • Embed the global operating model across EMEA, ensuring standards, processes, tools and governance expectations are adopted consistently.
  • Translate enterprise-level standards into practical, market-specific ways of working.

Resource and capacity management

  • Own the regional view of demand, supply, utilisation, resource mix and capacity gaps.
  • Partner with Global Capacity Management, Account Teams, Delivery Leads and Offshore Operations to optimise deployment, resolve constraints and improve utilisation.
  • Provide regional input into enterprise workforce planning and future capacity needs.

Business and client enablement

  • Ensure regional client teams have the operational foundations needed to mobilise and deliver work effectively.
  • Coordinate core business processes including client onboarding, timesheeting, billing readiness, interagency set-ups, compliance and headcount approvals.
  • Act as the regional operational point of coordination for enablement issues, working across Finance, HR, Technology and Implementation to unblock dependencies.

Commercial performance and margin management

  • Manage the operational levers that affect cost-to-serve across the region, including scope leakage, resource efficiency, rework and avoidable cost.
  • Partner with Account Leadership and Finance to improve margin visibility and ensure practical actions are in place to protect profitable delivery.
  • Oversee regional budget performance and present financial outcomes to regional and global stakeholders.

Regional insight and continuous improvement

  • Use performance data to identify risks, issues and improvement opportunities across the region.
  • Translate insight into action — ensuring key issues have clear owners, measurable outcomes and appropriate escalation routes.
  • Identify recurring operational bottlenecks and lead remediation, including regional adoption of global improvement initiatives.

Cross-functional partnership

  • Act as the key operational connector between EMEA and global operations capabilities.
  • Partner across Sales, Account, Implementation, Finance, HR, Technology and Offshore functions to drive client outcomes and operational consistency.
  • Provide regional operational input into sales pursuits, client mobilisation, scope expansions and solution design — ensuring proposed models are deliverable and scalable.
  • Interface with Global Programme Directors where regional and global client contexts intersect, aligning on dependencies, escalations and capacity impacts.

Team leadership and development

  • Lead, coach and develop the Regional Operations team, building a high-performing function with clear roles, standards and ways of working.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational discipline and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure the team has the skills, confidence and behaviours needed to support a more mature, insight-led and scalable delivery model. 

What you need to be great in this role: 

Essential

  • Senior operations leadership experience within, advertising, consulting, creative production, media agency or professional services.
  • Deep understanding of agency operating models — including client delivery, workflow, resource planning, utilisation, scopes of work, billing, compliance and margin management.
  • Proven experience leading regional or multi-market operations teams in a people-led, fast-paced environment.
  • Strong commercial acumen, with confidence managing the operational levers that affect profitability.
  • Experience owning or improving resource and capacity management, including demand and supply visibility, workforce mix and deployment planning.
  • Ability to use operational data, KPIs and reporting to identify risks, drive action and improve performance.
  • Track record embedding governance, process discipline and ways of working across complex teams or markets.
  • Strong cross-functional stakeholder skills — with experience partnering across regional and global functions including Finance, HR, Technology, Account and Delivery.
  • Proven people leadership: building capable teams, strengthening operational performance and creating a culture of accountability.
  • Comfortable moving between strategic direction and hands-on operational problem-solving.

Desirable

  • Experience in a global matrix organisation with regional, global and offshore delivery models.
  • Background in an in-house agency, embedded agency, creative production or complex marketing ecosystem.
  • Exposure to client mobilisation, implementation, transition or new operating model design.
  • Experience contributing to RFPs, commercial modelling, solution design or delivery model development.
  • Exposure to automation, AI-enabled operations, workflow optimisation or digital transformation in a marketing or agency environment.

Commercial and budget accountability

  • Experience overseeing regional or annual operational budgets and presenting financial performance to senior stakeholders.
  • Track record of driving margin discipline — reducing leakage, rework and avoidable cost across complex delivery environments.
  • Ability to connect operational decisions to commercial outcomes and communicate financial performance clearly to leadership.
  • Strategic integration of AI tools to improve operational efficiency, insight and reporting across a regional function.
  • Experience setting AI governance standards and embedding AI-assisted workflows within a team or function.
  • Agentic leadership approach: systematic, outcome-oriented problem-solving across complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Confidence driving AI adoption and sharing best practice across a broader operations network.

In this role, you'll help us build and scale our server-driven UI ( SDUI ) platform, enabling teams to build a UI once and have it deploy seamlessly to iOS, Android, and Web without redeploying a new app — performantly and consistently. This role is based in our London office with a hybrid setup, typically three days in the office. What You'll Be Doing You'll be joining the SDUI team. We own the Android rendering layer of our server-driven UI platform, and the backend services that drive it, ensuring every consumer surface built on it is fast, correct, and visually indistinguishable from native. Here's what your day-to-day might look like: Drive technical execution by designing, building, and evolving the Android SDUI renderer — and the backend services (Kotlin, Golang, Protobuf) that feed it — to handle complex, real-time UI updates at scale. Lead architectural improvements and code reviews, ensuring the maintainability, visibility, and operational health of the renderer as more teams build on top of it. Partner with cross-functional disciplines (iOS and Web renderer engineers, product and design teams) to plan rollouts, align on platform decisions, and influence the roadmap. Own large-scale initiatives from design to delivery — including the push to bring SDUI motion and interaction quality to native-equivalent, and the ongoing migration off legacy rendering systems.   • Drive technical execution by designing, building, and evolving the Android SDUI renderer — and the backend services (Kotlin, Golang, Protobuf) that feed it — to handle complex, real-time UI updates at scale.

  • Lead architectural improvements and code reviews, ensuring the maintainability, visibility, and operational health of the renderer as more teams build on top of it.

  • Partner with cross-functional disciplines (iOS and Web renderer engineers, product and design teams) to plan rollouts, align on platform decisions, and influence the roadmap.

  • Own large-scale initiatives from design to delivery — including the push to bring SDUI motion and interaction quality to native-equivalent, and the ongoing migration off legacy rendering systems.

About Deliveroo Our mission is to transform the way people shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of one of the most rapidly expanding industries in the world: a complex, always-on, three-sided marketplace that impacts millions of people every day. Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. The Team BizOps is the team that keeps its finger on the pulse of business performance: continuously, rigorously, and across multiple dimensions at once. We turn raw operational and financial data into actionable intelligence, surfacing what is happening, why it is happening, and what to expect next , for the operators, executives, and functional teams who run the business day to day. We are not a reporting function that produces outputs on request. We work continuously, proactively watching, delivering, and questioning whether the signal is real, acting as "first responders" to surprising deviations from expectation and using what we learn to drive faster, better decision-making for the business at large. Our work spans the full stack of analytics: from the warehouse models that make metrics trustworthy, to the monitoring systems that catch problems early, to the reports and dashboards that make performance visible, to the deep-dive investigations that explain what the numbers mean and what we should do about it. We anchor our analysis to the right reference points: how performance compares to plan, to prior periods, and to what we'd expect, and we bring causal rigour when the business needs to know whether an action actually worked. The culture within the team is informal, fast-paced and entrepreneurial. Given the growth of the business and the level of senior stakeholder exposure, progression in the team can be fast. The Role Deliveroo is hiring a Senior Data Scientist to join BizOps, based in our London HQ (hybrid, minimum three days per week in the office). This role is largely project-based: starting from a strategic or performance question, you'll combine data, business context, and structured problem-solving to provide the insights that drive decision-making at a global level with senior stakeholders. You will own delivery end-to-end, from the messy, ambiguous question to a rigorous, trustworthy, and actionable answer. You'll be equally comfortable building the systems that make performance visible and going deep on the investigations that explain it. One week you might diagnose why a key market has moved away from plan; the next, identify the drivers behind a change in customer or operational performance; the next, build monitoring that helps teams spot and understand emerging issues earlier. Success in this role requires building effective working relationships across Deliveroo, particularly with international markets, as well as the Data Science, Operations, Commercial, and Finance teams.   What You'll Be Doing Answer the questions that matter, continuously. Maintain a rigorous view on business performance: Are we on track against our goals? What's changed? How does this compare with what we expected? What should we expect next? Then go further: Why is it happening, what matters most, and what should we do about it?" Own delivery end-to-end. Independently identify, define, and deliver impactful work aligned with business goals, operating with minimal guidance to ship fast, high-quality solutions. Navigate ambiguity. Deconstruct broad, ambiguous problem spaces into structured analytical roadmaps, and understand how your work intersects with adjacent systems and teams. Build for scale, not one-offs. Build the pipelines, models, dashboards, monitoring, and investigative tooling that make performance visible and reliable. Automate wherever possible; redoing analyses by hand is slow and error-prone. Measure impact with discipline. Design measurement strategies from simple A/B tests to quasi-experimental designs (synthetic control, difference-in-differences, event studies) when trials aren't feasible, always with conservative, assumption-explicit language. Be a first responder. Surface deviations before they become escalations, and be just as willing to give the confident "this is noise, no action needed" as the alarm. Communicate to influence. Translate complex findings into clear, simple, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences that shape roadmaps and decisions. Raise the bar. Contribute to the broader Analytics community, improve shared approaches and best practices, and help build data literacy across the business. What You'll Need to Thrive Our ideal candidate brings strong expertise in some of these areas and the curiosity to grow in others: Experience in an analytical or data science role, such as data analytics, data science, forecasting, planning, strategy analytics, or a similar discipline. Experience in logistics, e-commerce, marketplaces, or another fast-moving, customer-focused business is useful but not essential. Proficiency with SQL and a scripting language such as Python or R, alongside experience with BI or visualisation tooling such as Looker, Tableau, or similar. Comfortable using modern AI-assisted tools to work efficiently while maintaining high standards of accuracy and reproducibility. A pragmatic approach to problem-solving: you can balance analytical rigour with speed, adapt your approach to the importance of the decision, and focus effort where it will have the greatest impact. Effective problem-solving: you can take an ambiguous question, identify the underlying problem or decision, develop hypotheses, and use data and business context to reach a clear point of view. Experience with experimentation and/or causal inference is a strong plus: the ability to unpick insights and steer strategic decisions. Excellent communication skills, in person, in writing, and in code, with the ability to translate business needs into analytical problems and complex findings into simple recommendations. Driven, hard-working, and agile. BizOps sits at the centre of a fast-growing business; we move quickly to scale at pace. London-based, with a minimum of three days per week in the office. Why Join Us? description: About the team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. OpenAI for Government (OAI4G) helps public-sector institutions understand, adopt, and deploy highly capable AI products in support of their missions. The team brings together Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, and other cross-functional partners to help governments use AI responsibly and effectively. As part of OAI4G’s International Public Sector team, you will help public institutions in the UK, Middle East (ME) and Latin America (LATAM) translate frontier AI into secure, compliant, mission-aligned outcomes. We work across varied procurement, regulatory, security, sovereignty, and commercial environments, while maintaining a consistent commitment to safety, reliability, and public benefit. About the role We are seeking a Global Account Director (GAD) to lead OpenAI’s public-sector work across the UK, ME and LATAM. You will build trusted relationships with government leaders, develop and execute account strategies, create and close complex opportunities, and help customers move from initial interest to successful adoption. This is a full-cycle, highly cross-functional sales role that combines technical understanding, strategic vision, partnership management, and value-driven execution. You will work with senior government, operational, technical, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders to identify high-impact AI use cases and translate them into credible commercial and deployment pathways across the OpenAI Platform API and Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise. You will also be an accountable customer leader after signature, working alongside specialist delivery and technical teams to keep customer outcomes, milestones, adoption, risks, and executive alignment on track. The role requires excellent judgement, executive presence, local fluency, and the ability to move between strategy, discovery, capture, procurement, delivery governance, and relationship management without day-to-day direction. This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will Own a focused portfolio of UK, ME and LATAM public-sector accounts. Build and execute comprehensive account plans that map mission priorities, stakeholders, procurement paths, partners, use cases, risks, and long-term expansion opportunities. Drive complex opportunities through the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation, discovery, qualification, capture, and commercial strategy through negotiation, closure, adoption, and expansion. Lead public-sector customers through their AI adoption journey, helping them identify responsible, high-impact use cases and connect mission outcomes to OpenAI’s capabilities and limitations. Translate between government leaders, end users, technical teams, policy and security stakeholders, and internal product and engineering partners, clearly communicating requirements, progress, risks, and dependencies. Serve as the accountable customer lead for engagements tied to clear outcomes, customer milestones, adoption measures, and commercial commitments, coordinating closely with technical specialists. Work closely with the Partnerships team, global and regional system integrators, cloud and technology providers, local delivery partners, resellers, and strategic international partners to shape joint pursuits, deployment models, and purchasing paths. Develop capture strategies, competitive positioning, win themes, teaming decisions, and proposal narratives that reflect UK, ME and LATAM market conditions. Navigate public-sector procurement, tendering, security, data-residency, compliance, and sovereignty requirements, bringing Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, Finance, and other partners into opportunities early. Build trusted relationships with senior government executives and decision-makers, while staying close to operational users and technical stakeholders whose workflows determine successful adoption. Maintain accurate pipeline, forecasting, account records, customer follow-up, and executive reporting, with disciplined follow-through across markets and time zones. Monitor the government, technology, procurement, partner, and competitive landscape across UK, ME and LATAM markets, surfacing insights that inform product roadmaps and go-to-market strategy. Represent OpenAI at government, partner, and industry forums, strengthening networks and identifying opportunities that advance responsible public-sector adoption of AI. We’re seeking someone with experience including 10+ years in government, diplomacy, national security, international development, multilateral institutions, public-sector technology sales, business development, consulting, transformation, systems integration, or a closely related field, with meaningful ownership of complex customer outcomes. Direct experience in government, diplomacy, national security, foreign affairs, or international organisations, or very significant experience working with those customers in sensitive, regulated, or high-consequence environments. Material experience operating credibly in sensitive or national-security-adjacent settings; an active or recently held government security clearance is valuable, and the ability to obtain or maintain any clearance required for the portfolio may be necessary. A strong record of shaping and closing complex cross-border deals: account planning, discovery, qualification, stakeholder mapping, capture, proposal development, negotiations, forecasting, closure, adoption, and expansion. Executive presence with senior diplomats, ministers, multilateral executives, government leaders, and decision-makers, alongside credibility with technical, operational, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders. Sound understanding of multilateral and public-sector procurement, funding, contracting, security, privacy, data-residency, sovereignty, and compliance requirements across more than one ME or LATAM market. Ability to orchestrate regional and international partners, including system integrators, resellers, cloud providers, development institutions, advisory partners, and delivery partners. Enough AI and enterprise-technology fluency to explain OpenAI’s products, capabilities, limitations, and responsible-use trade-offs clearly to diplomatic, multilateral, and government audiences, and to engage the right specialists early. High ownership, exceptional written and verbal communication, diplomatic judgement under ambiguity, strong capacity management across regions and time zones, and willingness to travel across ME and LATAM, and internationally as needed. Nice to have Deep relationships across international organisations, regional bodies, development institutions, foreign affairs, defence, national security, or other sensitive public-sector communities. Experience developing opportunities across more than one ME or LATAM market, ideally with exposure to international organisations or regional bodies. Experience with AI/ML, cloud, data platforms, cybersecurity, API-based products, public-sector digital transformation, or regulated cross-border technology deployments. Experience moving a complex cross-border opportunity from early mission discovery through procurement, deployment governance, adoption, and measurable outcomes. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information.   • Lead our EMEA complaints reviews: Run our monthly complaints meetings, bringing visibility to trends, volumes and priorities across the region

  • Drive root cause analysis: Work cross-functionally with internal teams to identify why issues occur, and lead the push for long-term fixes rather than one-off resolutions

  • Help build our complaints AI capability: As volumes grow, help shape how we use AI to handle complaints more efficiently at scale

  • Strong working knowledge of DISP and other relevant complaints-handling regulation

  • A track record of meeting productivity and quality targets in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment

By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.</p></div><h2><strong>What is The Role:</strong></h2> <p>As part of the Platform Engineering department, the SRE team is designing, building, scaling and maturing the multi-cloud platform for hosting internal and external services such as the Elastic Cloud<a href="https://www.elastic.co/cloud" target="_blank"> Hosted</a> and<a href="https://www.elastic.co/elasticsearch/serverless" target="_blank"> Serverless</a>. We develop and extend new software and tools that support the rest of the infrastructure, so that we can rapidly deploy products from all corners of Elastic. We want your experience and recommendations to offer a truly exceptional customer experience!</p> <h2><strong>What you will be doing:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Taking an engineering approach in leading technical initiatives for automating system engineering efforts to guarantee the reliability of the global Elastic infrastructure. .</li> <li>Growing our global Platform infrastructure to meet the increasing scaling demands by developing and maintaining software, tooling and automations.</li> <li>Using an inclusive approach at championing an environment focused on collaboration, operational excellence, and uplifting others.</li> <li>Responding to and preventing repeated customer impact in response to major incidents and prioritised problem management. Our on call rotation uses follow-the-sun model where everyone participates in it in (mostly) their working hours.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you bring:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Success and lessons of experiences from striving for 'progress not perfection' in the name of Platform reliability. We want to hear about your customer first approach in solving operational problems with a SRE perspective.</li> <li>A background in software engineering to collaborate with engineers to expertly identify, implement and deliver solutions. An experience in public cloud and managed Kubernetes services is advantageous.</li> <li>Passion for developing solutions that involve inclusive communication methods to grow and strengthen partner and team relationships. Examples of working in distributed teams or working remotely is desirable.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Bonus Points:</strong></h2> <p>You don't need to have all of these items, but these represent the types of work you will do as a Site Reliability Engineer at Elastic.</p> <ul> <li>You have operated a SaaS product in a public cloud ideally built using Infrastructure-as-Code tooling such as Crossplane or Terraform</li> <li>You have built or operated a Kubernetes-at-scale infrastructure, ideally across multiple cloud providers, and the vital automation to support it.</li> <li>You have written non-trivial programs in Golang or other programming languages.</li> <li>You have worked with containerized services (such as Docker.)</li> <li>You have proven experience in leading and improving alerting and major incident management standard processes metrics systems (e.g. Elastic Stack, Graphite, Prometheus, Influx) to diagnose issues and quantify impacts to present to others at varying level of the organization.</li> <li>You have experience in system administration with professional skills in Linux on distributed systems at scale.</li> <li>You have diagnosed or designed, implemented and created solutions with the Elastic Stack.</li> <li>You are experienced in thriving in a self-organizing and sharing in a globally distributed team environment.</li> <li>You strengthen team members in bringing out the best of each other by uplifting others with coaching and mentoring.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h2><strong>Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People</strong></h2> <p>As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.</p> <p>We strive to have parity of benefits across regions and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do.</p> <ul> <li>Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary</li> <li>Health coverage for you and your family in many locations</li> <li>Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles</li> <li>Generous number of vacation days each year</li> <li>Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service</li> <li>Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love</li> <li>Embracing parenthood with minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave</li> </ul> <p>Different people approach problems differently. raw.title: Partner Acquisition Specialist
raw.description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice.

By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we’ve transformed how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of Europe’s largest car-changing destinations. Over 10 million customers have used carwow to buy and sell cars, with £3bn worth of cars bought and £1.8bn listed for sale last year alone.

In 2024, we acquired Autovia — creators of Auto Express and evo — doubling our audience overnight. Today, our brands reach over 350 million users annually and generate 1.1bn+ YouTube views, influencing how millions of drivers choose their next car.

And we’re a long way from done.

GYC ADVERTISING @ CARWOW

This role sits within GYC (Get Your Car) Advertising, a fast-growing commercial team responsible for building Carwow’s Used and New Car Advertising business.

The two markets are at very different stages:

  • New Car Advertising is a mature, high-performing product with strong market fit and limited competition.

  • Used Car Advertising is an emerging channel — competitive, fast-moving, and still being proven.

We operate like a startup within a startup:

  • small team

  • high ownership

  • evolving products and processes

  • limited structure by design

As a BDR, you’ll help build the foundations of this business by creating high-quality outbound pipeline, shaping how we approach dealers, and defining what “good” looks like from the ground up.

YOUR MISSION

Your mission is to create qualified pipeline from cold outbound outreach, focused initially on Used Car Advertising, and set the sales team up to win.

This role is not about closing deals or working warm leads.

It’s about discipline, resilience, and learning — building strong sales fundamentals in a fast-moving, high-accountability environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Generate outbound pipeline (Used-first)

  • Cold-call and message independent dealers and retail groups

  • Open relevant commercial conversations about Used Car Advertising

  • Book qualified meetings only for BDMs

Qualify before you book

  • Ask structured discovery questions

  • Understand dealer context (stock size, sales velocity, appetite to invest)

  • Disqualify early when there’s no fit

Build strong sales fundamentals

  • Learn how carwow demand works

  • Develop an understanding of used-car dealer economics

  • Improve messaging and objection handling through repetition and feedback

Operate with discipline

  • Hit clear daily and weekly activity targets

  • Maintain accurate CRM records

  • Protect BDM time by avoiding low-quality meetings

KEY REQUIREMENTS

  • Comfortable with cold outreach and rejection

  • Clear, concise communicator

  • Able to follow structure and process consistently

  • Curious about how businesses make money

  • Coachable and open to feedback

  • Resilient and focused under pressure

BONUS POINTS

  • Previous outbound sales or customer-facing experience

  • Exposure to automotive, marketplaces, or performance-led products

  • Desire to progress into more senior commercial roles over time

WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU

  • If you’re looking for inbound or warm leads

  • If you dislike repetition and outbound activity

  • If you prefer closing over qualifying

  • If you need heavy structure and certainty from day one

FINAL NOTE

This role is ideal if you want to learn outbound sales properly, build real commercial skills, and progress over time into broader Used and New Car Advertising roles.

If you’re resilient, curious, and ready to build from scratch, we’d love to talk.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Talent Screen (20–30 min)

title: Labour AI Specialist
description: About Sona Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment. Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. We think that's because the problem needed AI, not just better software, before it was solvable. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. title: Senior Product Manager (JetBrains Context)
description: <p>Coding agents are only as good as the context they're given. Most explore a repository like a new hire on day one – grepping, opening files, guessing. JetBrains Context replaces that with actual knowledge of your whole codebase and resources, served to any agent that asks. If you want to own the layer that decides what an agent knows before it writes a single line, this is for you.</p> <h2><strong>About JetBrains</strong></h2> <p>We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <p>As agents get better at searching for themselves, what is the durable value of a managed retrieval layer? We need someone with an opinionated answer to own JetBrains Context as a product – defining what it is for, who it is for, how we measure success, and where it goes next.</p> <p>This is a hands-on role where you'll manage the product from a terminal and agent session rather than slides. You'll bridge the technical core and cross-functional teams: collaborating closely with engineering and ML teams on indexing pipelines and retrieval quality, working with Air, IDE, and Junie teams on integrations, and partnering with marketing, developer advocacy, sales, and customer success on positioning and adoption. You'll take full ownership of defining problem statements, setting explicit trade-offs, and balancing cost, latency, and freshness across the platform.</p> <p>Day to day, you will:</p> <ul> <li>Build and maintain a deep working understanding of chunking, embeddings, index freshness, retrieval, reranking, and agent-facing surfaces.</li> <li>Define and defend an opinionated vision for the product's evolution, including explicit target audiences, use cases, and key success metrics.</li> <li>Translate product strategy into actionable problem statements, priorities, plans, and milestones with an explicit definition of “done”.</li> <li>Communicate product direction clearly to engineering, leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, customers, and prospects.</li> <li>Analyze competing context and code-search products through direct use to establish clear differentiators and identify gaps.</li> <li>Define core operational and product metrics – index freshness, retrieval quality, agent task outcomes, adoption, retention, and unit economics – to guide decision-making.</li> <li>Represent the product externally by sharing roadmaps, publishing updates, speaking to developer audiences, and gathering community feedback.</li> <li>Partner with ML teams on model evaluation and platform teams on service scale, reliability, and cost.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A well-argued point of view on where AI-first development is going and what agents genuinely need from a context layer.</li> <li>Comfort with technical depth across embeddings, retrieval quality, sub-agents, tool-calling, indexing costs, and API design.</li> <li>The habit of using the product you build daily alongside competitors' tools.</li> <li>Communication that adapts to different audiences, from staff engineers and enterprise architects to conference attendees.</li> <li>A data-informed approach that combines telemetry, evaluation results, customer conversations, and market signals.</li> <li>Comfort with ambiguity and a preference for defining a new category over copying an existing one.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll need</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Proven experience owning a complex developer, platform, or infrastructure product end to end, including strategy and roadmap.</li> <li>Hands-on familiarity with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows.</li> <li>The technical capability to work directly with engineering on retrieval behavior, APIs, data models, and integration surfaces.</li> <li>The ability to define metrics for quality-sensitive products and build evaluation habits that maintain product standards.</li> <li>Experience communicating a product externally through written content, talks, or community engagement.</li> <li>Practical experience with search, retrieval, RAG, developer search, or static analysis at scale is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What success looks like</strong></h2> <p>Within your first months, you'll form and share a clear thesis for what JetBrains Context is and is not – one the engineering team recognizes as theirs and leadership can invest in. You'll establish a metrics story that distinguishes real retrieval quality from vanity usage, a roadmap with clear trade-offs, and a documented evaluation of serious competitors.</p> <p>Longer term, success means JetBrains Context becomes a deliberate choice for developers and organizations, agents get measurably better answers because it exists, enterprises adopt it for its governance and scale, and the market clearly understands its unique value because you've communicated it effectively.</p> <p><strong><br><br>Why join JetBrains?&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong base salary. title: Staff Product Security Architect
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values&nbsp;and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>We are hiring a Staff Product Security Architect to join our Security Platforms and Architecture organization at GitLab.</p> <p>Rather than operating as a purely consultative body, Security Architecture at GitLab functions as a hands-on technical driver. Our mission is to embed proactive guidance directly into modern developer workflows and automated coding environments, embedding security standards into the software development process from the outset. We strive to enable teams to deliver secure, resilient software seamlessly while minimizing reliance on manual security gates.</p> <p>In this role, you will collaborate closely with product engineering organizations, spearhead architectural strategy for critical capabilities, and serve as the primary Security Owner driving risk reduction for key entries within our risk management framework. Your daily work will span architectural design reviews, technical prototyping, and establishing scalable patterns that enable engineering teams to execute autonomously.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong>&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Partner with engineering and product leadership across GitLab, developing enough context in their domains to anticipate security problems rather than react to them</li> <li>Lead security architecture and design work for strategic initiatives, and provide direction to the cross-functional teams delivering them</li> <li>Identify, assess, and prioritise systemic security risks, and act as Security Owner for high-priority items in the Product Security Risk Register, co-executing remediation with the teams who own the code</li> <li>Codify recurring security decisions into reusable artifacts — guardrails, standards, design patterns,skills, and reference threat models — delivered into developer and AI coding tool workflows</li> <li>Build proofs of concept and prototypes to unblock engineering teams and shorten the distance between a security requirement and a working implementation</li> <li>Conduct security architecture reviews for large or strategic projects, and coordinate with Application Security so that review coverage is comprehensive and correctly prioritised</li> <li>Threat model new and existing systems, and establish the patterns that let teams threat model their own work</li> <li>Work with Security Research on proactive exploration of unknown risks in GitLab's architecture</li> <li>Anticipate emerging security challenges and propose architectural responses before they reach implementation</li> <li>Mentor security engineers across the division, and represent security architecture to engineering audiences</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll bring&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Depth in application security architecture, including authentication and authorization models, privilege escalation, multi-tenant isolation, and trust boundary analysis</li> <li>Experience securing distributed systems, including service-to-service authentication, secrets handling, and the failure modes of security decisions made across process boundaries</li> <li>Working knowledge of software supply chain security: build and release integrity, artifact provenance, and dependency risk</li> <li>A track record of proactive architecture work — identifying risk before it becomes an incident, and designing something that prevents a class of problem rather than an instance of one</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with engineering leadership and influence technical direction through expertise rather than gatekeeping</li> <li>Experience defining security standards or patterns that teams adopted without being compelled to</li> <li>The ability to operate strategically while remaining hands-on, including reading unfamiliar code, building prototypes, and contributing changes</li> <li>Clear written communication, and the ability to make a security argument to an engineering audience that does not already agree with it</li> <li>A view on how security guidance should be authored and delivered for AI coding tools, not only for humans</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>Security Architects are a part of our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/">Security Platforms and Architecture</a> team, who address complex security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. Composed of <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/security-architecture/">Security Architecture</a>, <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/security-research/">Security Research</a>, and Application Security, we focus on systemic product security risks and work cross-functionally to mitigate them while maintaining Engineering’s development velocity.</p> <p>In FY27, we're implementing a new organizational model where each architect is dedicated to a specific functional area of GitLab's product, enabling deeper context, stronger relationships, and more proactive security guidance. As the Core DevOps architect, you'll be part of a team that includes architects focused on AI and the Sec Section, creating opportunities for collaboration on cross-cutting security challenges while maintaining specialized expertise in your domain.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the&nbsp;United States only. title: Thruster CAD and Stress Analyst
description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours. We want you as a talented CAD & Stress Analyst to help us in our mission by designing and structurally justifying the hardware that makes up our propulsion systems, with a particular focus on the Thrust Chamber Assembly(TCA). You will own parts from initial CAD layout through to final stress justification, working hand in hand with the manufacturing and test teams to bring flight hardware from concept to qualified design. Key responsibilities In your capacity as a CAD & Stress Analyst, you will be responsible for the on-time and on-cost design and structural justification of propulsion hardware, with the TCA as your primary scope. Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include: During the Design Phase: Design the thrust chamber & injector propulsion hardware in CAD, from concept layout through to detailed design. Perform stress analysis (hand calculations and FEA) on designed parts to substantiate margins of safety under mechanical, thermal and pressure loads. Select materials and define manufacturing processes in coordination with manufacturing engineering, accounting for structural, thermal and producibility constraints. Work closely with propulsion, thermal and fluidic system engineers to translate functional requirements into part-level design and load cases. Establish and maintain interface definitions, drawings and part datasets, ensuring configuration control and traceability. Conduct trade studies on design options (geometry, material, manufacturing route) and justify design decisions with analysis. Elaborate and maintain structural analysis reports supporting design reviews and qualification. Support the definition of test requirements needed to validate analytical models and structural assumptions. Produce and maintain technical documentation of design choices and trade-offs, to a high standard, capturing analysis methods and results as to serve as reference justification for the design. During Manufacturing, Assembly and Test Phase: Support manufacturing and inspection of parts, resolving design or tolerance issues as they arise. Support root-cause investigations of any structural anomaly or test finding, correlating analysis with hardware behaviour. Update and correlate stress models and analyses based on test and inspection results. Support design iterations and upgrades based on test campaign outcomes. What we would love to see from you A minimum of a bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering or similar degrees. Over 1 year of related experience in CAD design and stress analysis of mechanical or structural hardware, ideally in a propulsion, aerospace or high-reliability environment. Strong CAD skills, able to take a part from concept to a fully detailed, manufacturable design. Solid grounding in structural/stress analysis, including hand calculations and FEA (e.g. Ansys, Abaqus, or equivalent). Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, additive manufacturing, welding/brazing) and their impact on design and structural performance. Nice to have: CFD experience, for thermal or flow-related analysis of propulsion hardware. Excellent collaboration skills for working effectively across departments. Fluency in English. Skills and Behaviours Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong analysis and problem-solving skills. Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks. Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done. Ability to communicate at all levels of the business. Demonstrates behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork. Space enthusiast, ready to change the European space industry. Why you should join us! What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable. All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible. If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc. title: Ingénieur·e en médiation scientifique et valorisation de la recherche
description: 1-     ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation. Le poste est rattaché au Département interdisciplinaire en sciences sociales (DI2S) rassemblant des enseignants chercheurs et enseignantes chercheuses en sciences de gestion, sociologie, économie et droit. Sur le campus de Nantes, les recherches sont focalisées sur l’analyse des transformations des organisations et des métiers dans des systèmes sociotechniques. Trois domaines d’investigation sont privilégiés : l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement. Le ou la candidate sera affilé·e au LEMNA (Laboratoire Économie et Management Nantes Atlantique). Plus précisément, le poste sera rattaché à la chaire RESOH [Recherche en Sécurité Organisations Hommes]. Les travaux de recherche, à l’interface de la sociologie et de la gestion, portent sur le fonctionnement des organisations à hauts risques. Partant de l’analyse du travail et des organisations de travail, il s’agit d’éclairer les dimensions socio-organisationnelles, managériales et institutionnelles contribuant à (ou empêchant) le maintien d’un niveau de fiabilité compatible avec les exigences de sécurité et de production. Les recherches de la chaire sont conduites en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Elles visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques fondées sur des enquêtes de terrain, mais également à favoriser leur mise en discussion, leur appropriation et leur mobilisation par les acteurs concernés. Dans ce contexte, la chaire souhaite renforcer ses capacités de valorisation, de diffusion et d’appropriation de ses travaux, auprès de ses partenaires actuels comme, plus largement, du monde socio-économique.   2-     MISSIONS En collaboration avec l’ensemble des enseignants-chercheurs de l’équipe (permanents et associés), les missions sont : 1-     Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire 2-     Structurer et valoriser les résultats des recherches de la chaire 3-     En favoriser l’appropriation par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne) 4-     Contribuer au rayonnement de la chaire auprès du monde socio-économique (volet externe)     3-     ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission       Participer à la dynamique collective de recherche au sein de la chaire ·     contribue activement aux réunions de coordination, espaces de discussion et séminaires de recherche (au sein de l’équipe de recherche RESOH et avec les partenaires)   2.     Valoriser et diffuser les résultats des recherches de la chaire ·     cartographie les principaux travaux, résultats et productions de la chaire ; ·     identifie les publics susceptibles d’être intéressés par ces résultats ; ·     analyse leurs besoins et leurs attentes ; ·     contribue à définir des stratégies de valorisation et de communication adaptées aux différents projets ; ·     contribue à l’organisation des événements scientifiques (journée d’étude, colloque, etc.) ; ·     transforme les résultats scientifiques en ressources accessibles à des publics non spécialistes, sans en perdre la rigueur, la nuance ni la portée scientifique (synthèses, notes de recherche, fiches thématiques, supports de présentation, contenus numériques ou autres formats adaptés aux publics visés).   3.     Favoriser l’appropriation des travaux de recherche par les partenaires industriels et institutionnels de la chaire (volet interne) ·     prépare et organise des restitutions de travaux ; ·     conçoit et anime des ateliers ou temps d’échange ; ·     prépare des supports adaptés aux préoccupations des partenaires ; ·     recueille leurs réactions, questions et besoins ; ·     fait remonter vers les chercheurs les questions et attentes exprimées par les partenaires ; ·     contribue à identifier les conditions favorisant l’appropriation des résultats.   4.     Contribuer au rayonnement de la chaire auprès du monde socio-économique (volet externe) ·     identifie des organisations, réseaux et acteurs susceptibles d’être intéressés par les travaux de la chaire ; ·     développe et entretient des relations avec des acteurs industriels, institutionnels et professionnels ; ·     identifie des événements pertinents ; ·     prépare la participation de la chaire à des événements professionnels et scientifiques ; ·     participe à l’organisation d’événements scientifiques de la chaire (colloque, conférence, journée d’étude) ·     contribue à développer de nouveaux formats de rencontre entre chercheurs et praticiens ; ·     participe à la constitution de communautés d’intérêt autour de certaines thématiques de recherche. Niveau de formation et/ou expérience minimums souhaité : ·     Doctorat ·     Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent ·     Diplôme Bac + 4 ou équivalent avec expérience professionnelle ≥ 4 ans Notamment dans les domaines suivants : ·     sociologie ; ·     sciences de gestion ; ·     science politique ; ·     sciences de l’information et de la communication ; ·     médiation ou communication scientifique ; ·     valorisation et transfert des connaissances.   Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables : ·     Une bonne compréhension du fonctionnement de la recherche académique ·     capacité à comprendre rapidement des travaux scientifiques complexes ; ·     capacité à identifier et synthétiser les principaux résultats d'une recherche : ·     aptitude à dialoguer avec des scientifiques et à respecter les exigences de rigueur scientifique.   Une expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants appréciée : ·     valorisation ou diffusion de résultats de recherche ; ·     médiation ou communication scientifique ; ·     transfert ou circulation des connaissances ; ·     relations entre recherche et monde socio-économique ; ·     gestion de projets de recherche ; ·     animation de réseaux de partenaires ; ·     organisation d’événements scientifiques ou professionnels ; ·     conseil ou accompagnement des organisations et des transformations.   Capacités et aptitudes : Valorisation et communication Excellentes qualités rédactionnelles ; Très bonnes capacités d’analyse et de synthèse Capacité à adapter un contenu scientifique à différents publics Aptitude à concevoir des supports de diffusion variés Maîtrise des outils numériques et bureautiques Relations partenariales Très bonnes qualités relationnelles Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs aux cultures professionnelles différentes Goût pour les fonctions d’interface Capacité à créer et entretenir un réseau professionnel Aptitude à animer des réunions, ateliers et temps d’échange Gestion de projet Autonomie et sens de l’initiative Capacité à gérer plusieurs activités en parallèle Aptitude à planifier et coordonner des actions Capacité à respecter des échéances et à produire des bilans Les candidatures de personnes issues de la recherche, de la valorisation et du transfert de connaissances, de la médiation scientifique, de la communication scientifique ou du conseil en organisation sont encouragées. INFORMATIONS COMPLÉMENTAIRES Collaboration étroite avec la responsable de la chaire, et l’équipe, ainsi qu’avec les partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Collaboration éventuelle avec les services de communication ou de relations partenariales de l’établissement. Des déplacements ponctuels, financés intégralement par la chaire, pourront être nécessaires pour rencontrer les partenaires ou participer à des événements scientifiques et professionnels. POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE : 👉 Environnement exceptionnel de travail : Intégrez le campus de Nantes, situé au cœur de la technopôle de La Chantrerie, offrant un cadre arboré, moderne et propice à l'innovation au bord de l'Erdre. 👉 Des défis intellectuels stimulants : Participez à la valorisation de la recherche en transformant des résultats complexes en ressources accessibles pour des publics variés (industriels, institutionnels, grand public). 👉 I mpact concret : Contribuez à renforcer le dialogue entre recherche et société, en favorisant l’appropriation des connaissances par les acteurs socio-économiques. LES PLUS : 🥗 Restauration collective sur place 🏃‍♀️ Offres de loisirs/sport 🚌 Prise en charge des transports en commun 🚴‍♂️ Forfait mobilité durable (pour le covoiturage ou les trajets en vélo) 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Complément familial 💶 Large gamme de prestations sociales 🖥️ Télétravail partiel possible 🌴 Nombreux congés    INDICATIONS DE REMUNERATION : 💰 Rémunération indicative : à partir de 33 748€ brut annuel, selon le profil et l’expérience (charges salariales réduites en secteur public).    POUR TOUS RENSEIGNEMENTS : Sur le contenu du poste : Stéphanie TILLEMENT – Enseignante-Chercheure en Sociologie : Sur les aspects administratifs/RH: Mélissandre MORVAN – Assistante recrutement   Date limite de candidature : 23/10/2026 Début du contrat : 01/01/2027 Entretien : au fil de l’eau   Mentions Légales  : Nature et durée du contrat : CDD 18 mois de droit public ou détachement sur contrat pour les fonctionnaires renouvelable Localisation du poste : IMT Atlantique campus de Nantes - 4 Rue Alfred Kastler, 44300 Nantes À usage interne : Catégorie –métier du poste : II R Catégorie et métier des personnes pouvant postuler : II : D, E, F, G, H, I, R III : J1, J2, K, L, M Les postes offerts au recrutement sont ouverts à toutes et tous avec, sur demande, des aménagements pour les candidates et candidats en situation de handicap Emploi ouvert aux titulaires de la fonction publique et/ou aux personnes contractuelles Toute candidature peut faire l’objet d’une enquête administrative Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow
